    SigDoTS: significance testing for spatial domains

    Source: R/SigDoTS-package.R
    SigDoTS-package.Rd

    Domain-detection methods divide a tissue section into spatial domains, but the number of domains comes from a parameter, not from a test. SigDoTS tests which of the proposed domains are supported by the data. Starting from more candidate domains than you expect (K0 of them), it arranges them in a tree by spatial adjacency and expression similarity and tests the splits of the tree from the top down, each against a model in which the part being split is a single domain, with the spatial correlation of the noise and the correlation between genes estimated from the data. The parts of the tree that are not split further are the domains; the probability that any of the kept splits is false is at most alpha.

    The functions

    • sigdots() runs the test; it takes an expression matrix and coordinates, a Seurat object or a SpatialExperiment object, and the number of candidate domains K0 (or your own candidate domains).

    • sigdots_control() holds the settings that rarely need changing.

    • sigdots_prepare() makes the expression matrix from a raw counts matrix.

    • print() and summary() (summary.sigdots()) show the split tree and the tests.

    • domains() gives the domain of every spot as a table; add_domains() writes it into a Seurat or SpatialExperiment object.

    • plot() (plot.sigdots()) draws the domains, the candidate domains, the tree and the spatial correlation.

    • sigdots_example is a small simulated dataset to try the package on.

    The tutorials: vignette("SigDoTS") (getting started), vignette("own-data") (your own data), vignette("faq") (errors, warnings and questions), vignette("how-it-works") (the method step by step). The website, with a real-data application, is at https://yan-lab-msu.github.io/SigDoTS/.
